title.zh: 小测：土壤、侵蚀和分水岭

intro.en: Read each question twice. Watch for traps!

canNow.en: I can now answer questions on soil, erosion and divides.
canNow.zh: 我现在可以回答关于土壤、侵蚀和分水岭的问题。

questions.q: Soil is a mixture of...
options: rock pieces, minerals and organic matter

why.en: Soil has rock pieces, minerals and organic matter (plus water and air).
why.zh: 土壤有岩石碎块、矿物和有机物（还有水和空气）。

only sand and water.en: Sand is only one kind of rock piece. Soil also has organic matter (humus) and minerals.
only sand and water.zh: 沙子只是一种岩石碎屑。土壤还有有机物（腐殖质）和矿物质。

only dead leaves.en: Dead leaves are only the organic part. Soil also needs rock pieces and minerals.
only dead leaves.zh: 落叶只是有机的部分，土壤还需要岩石碎屑和矿物质。

only rocks.en: Rocks alone make gravel, not soil. Soil also needs organic matter from living things.
only rocks.zh: 只有石头是碎石，不是土壤。土壤还需要来自生物的有机物。

questions.q: Humus comes from...

why.en: Bacteria and fungi break down dead plants and animals into humus.
why.zh: 细菌和真菌把死去的植物和动物分解成腐殖质。

melted ice.en: Melted ice is just water. Humus is ORGANIC: it comes from things that were once alive.
melted ice.zh: 融化的冰只是水。腐殖质是有机物，来自曾经活着的东西。

weathered rock.en: Weathered rock makes the rock pieces in soil, not humus. Humus comes from living things.
weathered rock.zh: 风化的岩石形成土壤里的岩石碎屑，不是腐殖质。腐殖质来自生物。

rainwater.en: Rainwater is not alive and does not rot. Humus is made when dead plants and animals decay.
rainwater.zh: 雨水不是生物，不会腐烂。腐殖质是死去的动植物腐烂后形成的。

questions.q: Which horizon is topsoil?

why.en: Topsoil is Horizon A, under the O layer of leaves.
why.zh: 表土是 A 层，在 O 层（落叶层）下面。

Horizon O.en: Horizon O is the very top layer of fallen leaves and humus (O = organic). Topsoil is just under it.
Horizon O.zh: O 层是最上面的落叶和腐殖质层（O = organic 有机）。表土在它下面。

Horizon B.en: Horizon B is subsoil, under the topsoil. It has clay and minerals washed down from above.
Horizon B.zh: B 层是底土，在表土下面，有从上面冲下来的黏土和矿物。

Horizon C.en: Horizon C is near the bottom: broken pieces of weathered rock, not topsoil.
Horizon C.zh: C 层在接近底部：风化的碎石块，不是表土。

questions.q: Which horizon is mostly pieces of weathered rock?

why.en: Horizon C is at the bottom: pieces of weathered rock.
why.zh: C 层在最下面：风化的岩石碎块。

Horizon A.en: Horizon A is topsoil, dark and full of humus, not mostly rock pieces.
Horizon A.zh: A 层是表土，颜色深，有很多腐殖质，不主要是碎石。

Horizon B.en: Horizon B is subsoil with clay and minerals. The rock pieces are deeper, in C.
Horizon B.zh: B 层是底土，有黏土和矿物。碎石更深，在 C 层。

Horizon O.en: Horizon O is fallen leaves and humus on top. It has almost no rock.
Horizon O.zh: O 层是最上面的落叶和腐殖质，几乎没有石头。

questions.q: Erosion means...
options: dropping rock and soil in a new place

why.en: Erosion is when water, wind or ice CARRIES rock and soil AWAY from a place. (E for Erosion, E for Exit.) Dropping it somewhere new is a different word: deposition.
why.zh: 侵蚀是水、风或冰把岩石和泥土从一个地方带走。把它们放到新地方是另一个词：沉积。

soil growing plants.en: Plants growing is not erosion. In fact plant roots STOP erosion by holding soil in place.
soil growing plants.zh: 植物生长不是侵蚀。其实植物的根会抓住土，阻止侵蚀。

rocks melting.en: Melting rock makes magma, deep underground. Erosion happens on the surface and moves pieces, it does not melt them.
rocks melting.zh: 岩石熔化形成岩浆，在地下深处。侵蚀发生在地表，是搬运碎块，不是熔化。

dropping rock and soil in a new place.en: That is DEPOSITION, the step after erosion. Erosion takes away; deposition drops.
dropping rock and soil in a new place.zh: 那是沉积，是侵蚀之后的一步。侵蚀是带走，沉积是放下。

questions.q: A river drops its sediment where it meets the ocean. This makes a...

why.en: A delta forms at the river mouth, like the Mississippi River delta.
why.zh: 三角洲在河口形成，比如密西西比河三角洲。

gully.en: A gully is a small channel CUT by running water. It is made by erosion (taking away), not by dropping sediment.
gully.zh: 冲沟是流水冲刷出来的小沟，是侵蚀（带走）形成的，不是沉积形成的。

divide.en: A divide is high land that separates two river systems, far from the river mouth.
divide.zh: 分水岭是分开两个水系的高地，离河口很远。

glacier.en: A glacier is a huge moving body of ice, not sediment left by a river.
glacier.zh: 冰川是一大块会移动的冰，不是河流留下的沉积物。

questions.q: Wind erosion is greatest in...

why.en: Deserts have little water to hold soil and few trees to block the wind.
why.zh: 沙漠里水少，留不住土；树少，挡不住风。

places with many trees.en: Trees block the wind and their roots hold the soil, so wind erosion is SMALL there.
places with many trees.zh: 树会挡风，树根会抓住土，所以那里的风蚀很小。

rainforests.en: Rainforests are wet and full of plants. Wet soil sticks together and plants protect it.
rainforests.zh: 雨林又湿又有很多植物。湿土会粘在一起，植物会保护它。

under the sea.en: There is no wind under the sea. Wind erosion needs moving air over dry ground.
under the sea.zh: 海底没有风。风蚀需要空气吹过干的地面。

questions.q: What is the force under ALL erosion and deposition?

why.en: Gravity makes water and ice move downhill and makes particles settle.
why.zh: 重力让水和冰往下流，也让颗粒沉下来。

wind.en: Wind is one agent of erosion, but not under ALL of it. Rivers and glaciers move without wind. Gravity pulls them all.
wind.zh: 风只是侵蚀的一种动力，不是全部。河流和冰川不靠风也会动，它们都是被重力拉动的。

magnets.en: Magnetism does not move soil or water downhill.
magnets.zh: 磁力不会把土和水拉到山下。

sunlight.en: Sunlight gives heat but does not pull anything downhill. Only gravity pulls everything down.
sunlight.zh: 阳光给热量，但不会把东西拉到山下。只有重力会把一切往下拉。

questions.q: A divide is...
options: a deep hole in the sea
a line of high land where water runs down one side or the other

why.en: Rain on a divide runs down one side or the other.
why.zh: 落在分水岭上的雨从一边或另一边流下。

a river mouth.en: A river mouth is where a river ENDS at the sea, at low land. A divide is HIGH land.
a river mouth.zh: 河口是河流流入大海的地方，在低处。分水岭在高处。

a deep hole in the sea.en: A deep hole in the sea is a trench. A divide is on land and is high.
a deep hole in the sea.zh: 海里的深沟是海沟。分水岭在陆地上，是高的。

a layer of soil.en: A layer of soil is a horizon. A divide is a ridge of high land.
a layer of soil.zh: 一层土是土层。分水岭是一条高地。

questions.q: Water from the EAST slopes of the Rocky Mountains runs toward the...

why.en: The Rocky Mountains are a divide. Rain on the EAST side flows east and south (into the Mississippi River system) and ends in the Gulf of Mexico.
why.zh: 落基山脉是分水岭。东边的雨水往东、往南流（进入密西西比河水系），最后流进墨西哥湾。

Arctic Ocean.en: The Arctic Ocean is far to the north. East-slope water flows south-east to the Gulf.
Arctic Ocean.zh: 北冰洋在很远的北边。东坡的水往东南流向墨西哥湾。

Indian Ocean.en: The Indian Ocean is on the other side of the world, near Asia and Africa.
Indian Ocean.zh: 印度洋在世界的另一边，靠近亚洲和非洲。

Pacific Ocean.en: The Pacific is WEST of the Rockies. Only the west slopes drain to the Pacific.
Pacific Ocean.zh: 太平洋在落基山脉西边，只有西坡的水流向太平洋。

items.text: Please ___ your book here to me.

why.en: Toward the speaker (to me): bring.
why.zh: 拿到说话人这里：bring。

items.text: Don't forget to ___ your umbrella when you go to school.

why.en: Away from home: take.
why.zh: 从家里带走：take。

items.text: There were ___ students in class today because of the rain.

why.en: You can count students: fewer.
why.zh: 学生可以数：fewer。

items.text: I drink ___ milk than my brother.

why.en: You cannot count milk: less.
why.zh: 牛奶不能一个一个数：less。

why.en: Comparing two people: than.
why.zh: 比较两个人：than。

items.text: We ate lunch, and ___ we went swimming.

why.en: What happened next (time): then.
why.zh: 接下来发生的事（时间）：then。

items.text: Emma was happy to ___ the gift from her friend.

why.en: Take it and say yes: accept.
why.zh: 接受：accept。

items.text: Everyone came to the party ___ James, who was ill.

why.en: But not James: except.
why.zh: 除了 James：except。

items.text: The bus had ___ left when we got to the stop.

why.en: Before now: already (one word).
why.zh: 已经：already（一个词）。

items.text: The cat sat ___ the two chairs.

why.en: Two things: between.
why.zh: 两样东西之间：between。

title.en: Quiz: Earth History and Ocean Floor

intro.en: Read each question twice. Watch for traps!

canNow.en: I can now answer questions on rock layers and the ocean floor.
canNow.zh: 我现在可以回答关于岩层和海底的问题。

questions.q: Earth formed about...

why.en: Billion, not million: about 4.6 billion years.
why.zh: 是十亿不是百万：大约 46 亿年。

46 years ago.en: 46 years ago is within your parents' lifetime. Earth is far, far older than people.
46 years ago.zh: 46 年前你爸妈都还在世。地球比人类老得多得多。

4.6 million years ago.en: A million is 1,000 times smaller than a billion. 4.6 million years is far too young for Earth.
4.6 million years ago.zh: 一百万比十亿小 1000 倍。460 万年对地球来说太年轻了。

4600 years ago.en: 4600 years ago the Egyptian pyramids were being built. Earth was already billions of years old.
4600 years ago.zh: 4600 年前人类正在建金字塔，那时地球已经几十亿岁了。

questions.q: Uniformitarianism says...
options: the processes changing Earth today also changed it in the past
all rocks are the same age

why.en: Uniform means same: same processes, then and now.
why.zh: uniform 是“相同”：过去和现在是同样的过程。

all rocks are the same age.en: Rocks are different ages; that is why superposition works. The theory is about PROCESSES being the same.
all rocks are the same age.zh: 岩石年龄不同，所以叠加原理才有用。这个理论讲的是“过程”一样。

Earth never changes.en: The opposite: Earth is always changing, slowly, by the same processes (erosion, deposition, volcanoes).
Earth never changes.zh: 正相反：地球一直在慢慢变化，用的是同样的过程（侵蚀、沉积、火山）。

only volcanoes change Earth.en: Many processes change Earth: rivers, wind, ice, earthquakes. Uniformitarianism includes all of them.
only volcanoes change Earth.zh: 改变地球的过程很多：河流、风、冰、地震。均变论包括所有这些。

questions.q: By the principle of superposition, the OLDEST layer is usually...

why.en: Superposition: layers of sediment pile up one on top of another, like a stack of homework. The first one laid down ends up at the BOTTOM, so the bottom layer is the oldest. ("Super" = above: younger layers sit above older ones.)
why.zh: 叠加原理：沉积层一层一层往上堆，像一叠作业。最先放下的在最下面，所以最底层最老。（super = 在上面：新的层在老的层上面。）

in the middle.en: The middle layer was laid down after the bottom one, so it is younger than the bottom.
in the middle.zh: 中间那层比底层晚形成，所以比底层年轻。

at the top.en: The top layer was laid down LAST, so it is the youngest, not the oldest.
at the top.zh: 最上层是最后形成的，所以最年轻，不是最老。

on the side.en: Layers stack up and down, not side to side. Age is read from bottom (old) to top (young).
on the side.zh: 岩层是上下叠的，不是左右排。年龄从下（老）往上（新）看。

questions.q: Magma cuts through four rock layers. The magma is...
options: the same age as the top layer

why.en: Cross-cutting: the layers had to be there first.
why.zh: 切割关系：岩层必须先存在。

the oldest rock.en: Magma can only cut through rock that is ALREADY there. So the layers are older and the magma is younger.
the oldest rock.zh: 岩浆只能切穿已经存在的岩石，所以岩层更老，岩浆更年轻。

older than all four layers.en: If the magma were older, the layers would have formed on top of it, not been cut by it.
older than all four layers.zh: 如果岩浆更老，岩层会堆在它上面，而不是被它切开。

the same age as the top layer.en: It cuts through the top layer too, so the top layer had to exist first. The magma is younger.
the same age as the top layer.zh: 它连最上层也切穿了，所以最上层要先存在，岩浆更年轻。

questions.q: An unconformity is a place where...

why.en: Uplift and erosion removed some layers.
why.zh: 抬升和侵蚀磨掉了一些岩层。

the sea is deepest.en: The deepest parts of the sea are trenches. An unconformity is a gap in the rock record.
the sea is deepest.zh: 海最深的地方是海沟。不整合是岩层记录里的缺口。

soil is thickest.en: Thick soil is about soil horizons, not missing rock layers.
soil is thickest.zh: 土壤厚是土层的事，不是岩层缺失。

magma cuts through.en: Magma cutting through is cross-cutting (an intrusion). An unconformity is layers that are MISSING because they were eroded.
magma cuts through.zh: 岩浆切穿是交切（侵入）。不整合是岩层被侵蚀掉了，缺了一段。

questions.q: The continental shelf is...
options: the gentle part nearest the shore

why.en: Shelf = gentle, near the shore, up to about 150 to 200 m deep.
why.zh: 大陆架 = 平缓，靠近海岸，水深最多约 150 到 200 米。

the deepest flat floor.en: The deep flat floor is the abyssal plain, far from shore.
the deepest flat floor.zh: 深而平的海底是深海平原，离岸很远。

the steep drop.en: The steep drop is the continental slope, after the shelf ends.
the steep drop.zh: 陡峭的下坡是大陆坡，在大陆架之后。

a trench.en: A trench is a deep V-shaped valley where one plate dives under another.
a trench.zh: 海沟是一个板块插到另一个下面形成的深深的 V 形谷。

questions.q: Which part of the margin is steep and goes down to about 4000 m?

why.en: The slope drops steeply. Submarine canyons cut into it.
why.zh: 大陆坡陡峭下降，海底峡谷切进去。

abyssal plain.en: The abyssal plain is flat and very deep, not steep.
abyssal plain.zh: 深海平原又平又深，不陡。

continental shelf.en: The shelf is the gentle, shallow part near the shore (to about 200 m).
continental shelf.zh: 大陆架是靠岸的平缓浅水区（大约到 200 米）。

continental rise.en: The rise is a gentle pile of sediment at the BOTTOM of the slope, not the steep part.
continental rise.zh: 大陆隆是在大陆坡底部的平缓沉积物堆，不是陡的部分。

questions.q: A passive margin, like the east coast of North America, has...
options: a wide shelf and no plate boundary nearby
a narrow shelf and a trench
a mid-ocean ridge on the beach

why.en: Passive = no plate boundary = wide shelf (100 km or more).
why.zh: 被动 = 没有板块边界 = 宽大陆架（100 千米或更多）。

a narrow shelf and a trench.en: That is an ACTIVE margin (like the west coast), where a plate boundary is close.
a narrow shelf and a trench.zh: 那是活动大陆边缘（像西海岸），附近有板块边界。

many volcanoes.en: Volcanoes come from plate boundaries. Passive means there is NO boundary nearby, so few volcanoes.
many volcanoes.zh: 火山来自板块边界。passive（被动）就是附近没有边界，所以火山很少。

a mid-ocean ridge on the beach.en: Mid-ocean ridges are in the middle of the ocean, thousands of kilometres from the beach.
a mid-ocean ridge on the beach.zh: 大洋中脊在大洋中间，离海滩几千公里。

questions.q: Deep-sea trenches form where...
options: ocean crust dives under continental crust

why.en: Trenches are at convergent boundaries. Ridges are at divergent ones (trap!).
why.zh: 海沟在汇聚边界，洋中脊在离散边界（陷阱！）。

rivers meet the sea.en: Where a river meets the sea, it drops sediment and builds a delta, not a trench.
rivers meet the sea.zh: 河流入海的地方会沉积，形成三角洲，不是海沟。

glaciers melt.en: Melting glaciers drop sediment. Trenches are made by plates, not ice.
glaciers melt.zh: 冰川融化会留下沉积物。海沟是板块造成的，不是冰。

plates move apart.en: Plates moving apart (divergent) make a RIDGE, where new crust rises. Trenches form where plates come together.
plates move apart.zh: 板块分开（分离型）形成洋脊，新地壳在那里升起。海沟在板块相撞的地方。

questions.q: Mid-ocean ridges are about how long?

why.en: They are Earth's longest continuous mountain range.
why.zh: 它们是地球上最长的连续山脉。

50 kilometers.en: 50 km is about a one-hour drive. Ridges wind around the whole planet, far longer.
50 kilometers.zh: 50 公里大约开车一小时。洋脊绕着整个地球，长得多。

4000 meters.en: 4000 m is about the DEPTH of the ocean floor, not the length of the ridge.
4000 meters.zh: 4000 米大约是海底的深度，不是洋脊的长度。

200 meters.en: 200 m is about how deep the continental shelf goes, not a length.
200 meters.zh: 200 米大约是大陆架的深度，不是长度。

intro.en: Use the "say it in full" test: you're = you are, it's = it is.
intro.zh: 用“展开说”检查法：you're = you are，it's = it is。

canNow.en: I can now fix your/you're, their/they're, its/it's and more.
canNow.zh: 我现在可以改正 your/you're、their/they're、its/it's 等错误。

questions.q: Choose the correct word: ___ coat is on the chair.

why.en: "Your" is a possessive word: it shows something BELONGS to you (your coat = the coat that belongs to you). Before a noun like "coat", use your.
why.zh: your 是物主词，表示东西属于你（your coat = 你的外套）。在 coat 这样的名词前面用 your。

You're.en: You're is short for "you are". Test: "You are coat is on the chair" makes no sense, so not you're.
You're.zh: you're 是 you are 的缩写。试试：You are coat is on the chair 说不通，所以不是 you're。

Yore.en: Yore is an old word meaning "long ago" (days of yore). It does not show belonging.
Yore.zh: yore 是古词，意思是“很久以前”，不表示所属。

You.en: "You" is a pronoun for a person. To show the coat belongs to you, English uses the possessive form: your.
You.zh: you 是代词。要表示外套是你的，要用物主形式 your。

questions.q: Choose the correct word: ___ going to the beach tomorrow.

why.en: They're = they are. Test by expanding: "They are going to the beach" makes sense, so the answer is they're.
why.zh: they're = they are。展开试试：They are going to the beach 说得通，所以用 they're。

There.en: There is a PLACE (over there) or starts "there is". "There going to the beach" has no subject doing the going.
There.zh: there 表示地方（那里）或用在 there is。There going to the beach 没有“去”的人。

Theyre.en: A contraction needs an apostrophe to show the missing letter: they + (a)re = they're.
Theyre.zh: 缩写要用撇号表示省掉的字母：they + (a)re = they're。

Their.en: Their shows belonging (their car). It must be followed by a noun, and "going" is not a thing they own.
Their.zh: their 表示所属（their car），后面要接名词，going 不是他们拥有的东西。

questions.q: Choose the correct word: The dog wagged ___ tail.

why.en: "Its" (no apostrophe) is possessive: the tail belongs to it (the dog). Like his and her, possessive pronouns have NO apostrophe.
why.zh: its（没有撇号）是物主词：尾巴是它（狗）的。和 his、her 一样，物主代词没有撇号。

it's.en: It's always means "it is" or "it has". Test: "The dog wagged it is tail" makes no sense.
it's.zh: it's 永远是 it is 或 it has。试试：The dog wagged it is tail 说不通。

its'.en: Its' is not a word in English. There is no apostrophe after its.
its'.zh: 英语里没有 its' 这个词。its 后面没有撇号。

it.en: "It" is the pronoun for the dog itself. To show the tail belongs to the dog, use the possessive: its.
it.zh: it 指狗本身。要表示尾巴是狗的，用物主形式 its。

questions.q: Choose the correct word: ___ the girl singing on stage?

why.en: Who's = who is. Test: "Who is the girl singing on stage?" makes sense, so who's.
why.zh: who's = who is。试试：Who is the girl singing on stage? 说得通，所以用 who's。

Who.en: "Who the girl singing?" has no verb. The sentence needs "is", which is hiding in who's.
Who.zh: Who the girl singing? 缺少动词。句子需要 is，is 就藏在 who's 里。

Whose.en: Whose asks who something BELONGS to (Whose bag is this?). We are not asking about belonging.
Whose.zh: whose 是问东西属于谁（Whose bag is this?），这里不是问所属。

Whos.en: A contraction needs an apostrophe for the missing letter: who + (i)s = who's.
Whos.zh: 缩写要用撇号表示省掉的字母：who + (i)s = who's。

questions.q: Choose the correct word: Sophie ___ to live in London.

why.en: "Used to" + verb talks about a habit or state in the PAST that is not true now. Sophie lived in London before; she does not now.
why.zh: used to + 动词 表示过去的习惯或状态，现在不是了。Sophie 以前住在伦敦，现在不住了。

use.en: "Use" is present tense. The fixed phrase for a past habit is "used to", with -d.
use.zh: use 是现在时。表示过去习惯的固定说法是 used to，要加 -d。

using.en: "Sophie using to live" has no proper verb. The -ing form needs am/is/are before it.
using.zh: Sophie using to live 缺少正确的动词。-ing 形式前面要有 am/is/are。

uses.en: "Uses" is present tense (she uses a pen). It does not make the past-habit meaning.
uses.zh: uses 是现在时（she uses a pen），不能表示过去的习惯。

questions.q: Choose the correct word: James ate ___ orange.

why.en: We choose a or an by the SOUND that starts the next word. "Orange" starts with a vowel sound (o), so an: an orange. ("An" makes it easier to say.)
why.zh: 用 a 还是 an 要看下一个词开头的读音。orange 以元音 o 开头，所以用 an：an orange。（an 读起来更顺。）

the an.en: We never use two articles together. Use one: an orange (or the orange).
the an.zh: 两个冠词不能一起用，只用一个：an orange（或 the orange）。

a.en: "A" goes before a consonant sound (a banana). Orange starts with a vowel sound, so an.
a.zh: a 用在辅音开头的词前（a banana）。orange 以元音开头，所以用 an。

one an.en: "One" and "an" both mean one; using both is repeating. Just: an orange.
one an.zh: one 和 an 都是“一个”，两个都用就重复了。只说 an orange。

questions.q: Which is correct?
options: Take the box off of the table.
Take the box off the table.
Take the box of off the table.
Take the box offen the table.

why.en: "Off" already means "away from", so it needs no extra "of". Take the box off the table.
why.zh: off 已经是“从……离开”的意思，后面不需要再加 of。Take the box off the table。

Take the box off of the table..en: "Off of" uses two prepositions where one is enough. "Of" adds nothing, so drop it.
Take the box off of the table..zh: off of 用了两个介词，一个就够了。of 是多余的，去掉。

Take the box of off the table..en: "Of off" is the wrong order and still has the extra "of". Only "off" is needed.
Take the box of off the table..zh: of off 顺序错了，而且还是多了 of。只要 off。

Take the box offen the table..zh: 英语里没有 offen 这个词。

questions.q: Which is correct?
options: Their are a lot of pandas here.
There are allot of pandas here.
There are alot of pandas here.
There are a lot of pandas here.

why.en: Two things to check. "There are" tells us something exists (there = a place or "there is/are"). And "a lot" is always TWO words, like "a little".
why.zh: 检查两点：There are 表示“有”（there 是地方或 there is/are）。a lot 永远是两个词，就像 a little。

Their are a lot of pandas here..en: "Their" shows belonging (their pandas). To say pandas exist here, use "There are".
Their are a lot of pandas here..zh: their 表示所属（their pandas）。要说这里有熊猫，用 There are。

There are allot of pandas here..en: "Allot" is a different verb meaning to share out. "A lot" (many) is two words.
There are allot of pandas here..zh: allot 是另一个动词，意思是分配。表示“很多”的 a lot 是两个词。

There are alot of pandas here..en: "Alot" is not a word. Write it as two words, like "a little": a lot.
There are alot of pandas here..zh: alot 不是一个词。要分开写，像 a little 一样：a lot。

questions.q: Which is correct?

why.en: "A" means ONE, so the noun after it must be singular: a long way (one way). That is why it is "way", not "ways".
why.zh: a 表示“一个”，后面的名词要用单数：a long way。所以是 way，不是 ways。

We walked a longs way..en: "Long" is an adjective, and English adjectives never take -s.
We walked a longs way..zh: long 是形容词，英语形容词不加 -s。

We walked along ways..en: "Along" means beside or following (along the river). It does not mean a big distance.
We walked along ways..zh: along 是“沿着”（along the river），不表示很远的距离。

We walked a long ways..en: "A" means one, so it cannot go with plural "ways". Correct: a long way.
We walked a long ways..zh: a 表示一个，不能和复数 ways 一起用。正确：a long way。

questions.q: Which is correct?

why.en: "This" already points to the book that is here, so we do not add "here". Normal order: This book (subject) + is (verb) + mine.
why.zh: this 已经指着这里的书，不用再加 here。正常顺序：This book（主语）+ is（动词）+ mine。

Here this book is mine..en: "Here" repeats what "this" already says, so it is extra.
Here this book is mine..zh: here 重复了 this 的意思，是多余的。

This here is book mine..en: The word order is mixed up and "here" is extra. Subject first: This book is mine.
This here is book mine..zh: 词序乱了，而且 here 多余。主语在前：This book is mine。

This here book is mine..en: "This here" is informal speech and repeats the idea twice. In writing: This book.
This here book is mine..zh: this here 是口语，意思重复了。书面语：This book。

title.zh: 作业：土壤、侵蚀和分水岭

intro.en: Read Main Book S1 to S3 first. Then do this. You can try again as many times as you like.
intro.zh: 先读主课本 S1 到 S3，再做（可以做很多次）。

canNow.en: I can now answer soil, erosion and divide questions on my own.
canNow.zh: 我现在可以自己回答土壤、侵蚀和分水岭的问题。

questions.q: Soil horizons from TOP to bottom are...

why.en: Read soil from the surface down: O (Organic: fallen leaves) on top, then A (topsoil), then B (subsoil), then C (broken rock), just above bedrock. It follows the alphabet going down, with O first.
why.zh: 从地面往下读：最上面 O（有机层：落叶），然后 A（表土）、B（底土）、C（碎石），下面是基岩。往下按字母顺序，O 在最前。

O, C, B, A.en: This puts topsoil (A) at the bottom. Topsoil is near the top, just under O.
O, C, B, A.zh: 这样把表土 A 放到最底下了。表土在上面，就在 O 下面。

A, B, C, O.en: O is the leaf layer that lies ON TOP of the soil, so it comes first, not last.
A, B, C, O.zh: O 是盖在土上面的落叶层，所以排第一，不是最后。

C, B, A, O.en: This is bottom to top. The question asks top to bottom.
C, B, A, O.zh: 这是从下到上。题目问的是从上到下。

questions.q: Which part of soil is organic?

why.en: Organic = made by living things. Humus comes from dead plants and animals.
why.zh: 有机 = 由生物形成。腐殖质来自死去的动植物。

rock pieces.en: Rock pieces come from weathered rock, which was never alive, so they are not organic.
rock pieces.zh: 岩石碎屑来自风化的岩石，岩石从没活过，所以不是有机的。

minerals.en: Minerals come from rock, not from living things.
minerals.zh: 矿物来自岩石，不是来自生物。

air.en: Air fills the spaces in soil, but it was never alive, so it is not organic.
air.zh: 空气填在土壤的空隙里，但它从没活过，所以不是有机的。

questions.q: Iron and aluminum compounds washed down by rainwater collect in...

why.en: Rainwater washes minerals down from A into B.
why.zh: 雨水把矿物从 A 层冲到 B 层。

Horizon O.en: O is the leaf layer on top. Water washes minerals DOWN, away from the top.
Horizon O.zh: O 是最上面的落叶层。水把矿物往下冲，离开上层。

Horizon A (topsoil).en: Rainwater washes minerals OUT of A and carries them down. They collect in the next layer, B.
Horizon A (topsoil).zh: 雨水把矿物从 A 层冲走带到下面，堆积在下一层 B。

Horizon C.en: C is weathered rock. Most of the washed-down minerals stop in B, above it.
Horizon C.zh: C 是风化的岩石。被冲下来的矿物大多停在它上面的 B 层。

questions.q: A mature soil has how many horizons?

why.en: Mature soil has four horizons. Younger soil has fewer.
why.zh: 成熟土壤有四层，年轻土壤更少。

three.en: Three horizons is a younger soil that has not developed all its layers yet.
three.zh: 三层是比较年轻的土壤，还没有长出所有的层。

two.en: Two horizons is a very young soil.

ten.en: Soil is described with only O, A, B and C. There are not ten horizons.
ten.zh: 土壤只用 O、A、B、C 来描述，没有十层。

questions.q: Rainwater running off land leaves an eroded path called a...

why.en: A gully can grow into a stream or river.
why.zh: 冲沟可以变成溪流或河。

trench.en: A trench is a very deep valley in the ocean floor, made by plates, not by rainwater.
trench.zh: 海沟是海底很深的谷，是板块造成的，不是雨水。

delta.en: A delta is land BUILT where a river drops sediment. A gully is land CUT away.
delta.zh: 三角洲是河流沉积堆出来的陆地。冲沟是被冲刷掉的。

dune.en: A dune is a hill of sand piled up by wind, not a path cut by water.
dune.zh: 沙丘是风堆起来的沙山，不是水冲出来的沟。

questions.q: Deposition means...
options: dropping sediment in a new place

why.en: Deposition builds land in a new place.
why.zh: 沉积让新的地方土地变多。

melting ice.en: Melting is a change from solid to liquid. Deposition is about where sediment ends up.
melting ice.zh: 融化是固体变液体。沉积讲的是沉积物最后停在哪里。

carrying sediment away.en: Carrying away is EROSION. Deposition is the next step: dropping it.
carrying sediment away.zh: 带走是侵蚀。沉积是下一步：放下。

breaking rock.en: Breaking rock into pieces is WEATHERING, the first step.
breaking rock.zh: 把岩石弄碎是风化，是第一步。

questions.q: Sand dunes are built when...
options: the wind slows down and drops sand

why.en: Slow wind cannot carry its load, so it drops the sand.
why.zh: 风变慢带不动，就把沙子放下。

a river reaches the sea.en: A river reaching the sea makes a delta, not dunes. Dunes are built by wind.
a river reaches the sea.zh: 河流入海形成三角洲，不是沙丘。沙丘是风堆的。

rain makes a gully.en: A gully is carved by water (erosion). Dunes are piled up (deposition).
rain makes a gully.zh: 冲沟是水冲出来的（侵蚀）。沙丘是堆起来的（沉积）。

a glacier melts.en: A melting glacier drops a mix of rocks and soil, not neat hills of sand shaped by wind.
a glacier melts.zh: 冰川融化留下的是石头和泥土的混合物，不是风吹成的整齐沙丘。

questions.q: Glaciers can...

why.en: Glaciers move boulders and carve valleys over time.
why.zh: 冰川推动巨石，时间久了刻出山谷。

stop gravity.en: Nothing can stop gravity. In fact gravity is what pulls glaciers downhill.
stop gravity.zh: 没有东西能阻止重力，其实正是重力把冰川往山下拉。

make magma.en: Magma is melted rock from deep underground. Glaciers are cold ice on the surface.
make magma.zh: 岩浆是地下深处熔化的岩石。冰川是地面上冷冷的冰。

build deltas in the desert.en: Deltas form where rivers meet the sea. Glaciers are in very cold places, not deserts.
build deltas in the desert.zh: 三角洲在河流入海处形成。冰川在很冷的地方，不在沙漠。

questions.q: Drainage basin means the same as...

why.en: The Word Watch says drainage basin and watershed mean the same.
why.zh: 词语小贴士说 drainage basin 和 watershed 意思一样。

divide.en: A divide is the high EDGE that separates two drainage basins, not the basin itself.
divide.zh: 分水岭是分开两个流域的高边界，不是流域本身。

delta.en: A delta is the land at a river's mouth, only a small part at the end of a basin.
delta.zh: 三角洲是河口的陆地，只是流域末端的一小部分。

glacier.en: A glacier is moving ice, not an area of land that drains into one river.
glacier.zh: 冰川是移动的冰，不是一片流进同一条河的土地。

questions.q: Water from the WEST slopes of the Appalachian Mountains flows into the...

why.en: The Appalachian Mountains are a divide. Water on the WEST side flows west into the Ohio and Mississippi Rivers, which end in the Gulf of Mexico. The east side flows to the Atlantic.
why.zh: 阿巴拉契亚山脉是分水岭。西坡的水往西流进俄亥俄河和密西西比河，最后流进墨西哥湾。东坡流向大西洋。

Arctic Ocean.en: The Arctic is far north. West-slope water flows south-west to the Gulf.
Arctic Ocean.zh: 北冰洋在很远的北边。西坡的水往西南流向墨西哥湾。

Atlantic Ocean.en: The Atlantic is EAST of the Appalachians. Only the east slopes drain to it.
Atlantic Ocean.zh: 大西洋在阿巴拉契亚山脉东边，只有东坡流向它。

Pacific Ocean.en: The Pacific is on the other side of the continent, past the Rocky Mountains.
Pacific Ocean.zh: 太平洋在大陆另一边，要过落基山脉。

intro.en: Read Main Book E1 first. Then do this. You can try again as many times as you like.
intro.zh: 先读主课本 E1，再做（可以做很多次）。

canNow.en: I can now choose the correct usage word on my own.
canNow.zh: 我现在可以自己选对用法词。

questions.q: (Bring / Take) this letter to the post office, please.

why.en: Bring = move something TOWARDS the speaker (here). Take = move something AWAY from the speaker (there). The post office is away from here, so take.
why.zh: bring = 把东西带到说话人这里。take = 把东西带离说话人，到那里去。邮局不在这里，所以用 take。

Brought.en: "Brought" is the past of bring. This is a request for now, and the letter is going away, not coming here.
Brought.zh: brought 是 bring 的过去式。这是现在的请求，而且信是被带走，不是带过来。

Taked.en: Take is irregular. Its past is "took", never "taked". And a request needs the base form: take.
Taked.zh: take 是不规则动词，过去式是 took，没有 taked。请求句要用原形 take。

Bring.en: Bring means towards the speaker. The letter is going AWAY to the post office, so take.
Bring.zh: bring 是带到说话人这里。信是带去邮局，离开这里，所以用 take。

questions.q: There are (fewer / less) cars on the road today.

why.en: Use "fewer" for things you can COUNT one by one (1 car, 2 cars). Use "less" for things you cannot count (less water, less time). Cars can be counted, so fewer.
why.zh: 可以一个一个数的东西用 fewer（1 car、2 cars）。不能数的用 less（less water、less time）。车可以数，所以用 fewer。

lesser.en: "Lesser" means less important (a lesser prize). It is not used for numbers of things.
lesser.zh: lesser 是“次要的”（a lesser prize），不用来说数量。

few.en: "Few" means a small number, but this sentence compares with another day, so we need the comparative: fewer.
few.zh: few 是“少数”，但这句话是和另一天比较，要用比较级 fewer。

less.en: "Less" is for things you cannot count, like water or time. Cars are countable, so fewer.
less.zh: less 用于不能数的东西，比如水、时间。车可以数，所以用 fewer。

questions.q: Tom runs faster (than / then) Ben.

why.en: "Than" is the word for COMPARING two things (faster than, bigger than). "Then" is about TIME (first this, then that).
why.zh: than 用来比较两样东西（faster than、bigger than）。then 是表示时间（先这样，然后那样）。

then.en: "Then" means next or at that time. We are comparing speed, so than.
then.zh: then 是“然后、那时”。这里在比较速度，所以用 than。

thane.en: A thane is an old word for a lord in history. It has nothing to do with comparing.
thane.zh: thane 是历史上的贵族头衔，和比较没关系。

that.en: "That" points to something (that book). After a comparative like faster, English always uses than.
that.zh: that 是指东西（that book）。faster 这样的比较级后面一定用 than。

questions.q: We (could have / could of) won the game.

why.en: After "could", "should" or "would" (modal verbs), English uses HAVE + past participle to talk about the past: could have won. In speech we say "could've", and that sounds like "could of", which is how the mistake happens.
why.zh: could、should、would（情态动词）后面要用 have + 过去分词 来说过去的事：could have won。说话时我们说 could've，听起来像 could of，所以才会写错。

could of.en: "Of" is a preposition (a cup of tea), not a verb. A modal verb must be followed by a verb, so "have". "Could of" is only how could've SOUNDS.
could of.zh: of 是介词（a cup of tea），不是动词。情态动词后面必须接动词，所以是 have。could of 只是 could've 的读音。

could has.en: After a modal verb like could, the next verb is always in its base form (have), never has, even with he or she.
could has.zh: could 这样的情态动词后面的动词永远用原形 have，不用 has，就算主语是 he 或 she 也一样。

could off.en: "Off" means away from (take it off). It is not a verb, so it cannot follow could.
could off.zh: off 是“离开”（take it off），不是动词，不能放在 could 后面。

questions.q: Share the sweets (between / among) the five children.

why.en: Use "between" for TWO people or things (between Tom and me). Use "among" for THREE or more, a group (among the five children).
why.zh: 两个人或东西之间用 between（between Tom and me）。三个或更多、一群里面用 among（among the five children）。

betwixt.en: Betwixt is a very old form of between. It is not used today, and it would still mean two.
betwixt.zh: betwixt 是 between 很古老的说法，现在不用了，而且也只指两个。

between.en: "Between" is for two. There are five children, a group of more than two, so among.
between.zh: between 用于两个。这里有五个孩子，多于两个，所以用 among。

inbetween.en: "Inbetween" is not a correct word for sharing; even "in between" means in the middle of two things.
inbetween.zh: inbetween 不是正确的用法；就算 in between 也是指两个东西中间。

questions.q: Mia wanted to know (why / how come) the shop was closed.

why.en: "Why" is the standard question word for a reason. "How come" means the same, but it is chatty spoken English, so in writing use why.
why.zh: why 是问原因的标准疑问词。how come 意思一样，但它是口语，书面语要用 why。

how come.en: "How come" is informal speech. In schoolwork and writing, use why.
how come.zh: how come 是口语。作业和书面语用 why。

for why.en: "For why" is not correct English. The word why already asks for the reason.
for why.zh: for why 不是正确的英语，why 本身就在问原因。

how comes.en: "How comes" is not correct in any form of English.
how comes.zh: how comes 在任何英语里都不对。

questions.q: The story (that / where) we read was about a fox.

why.en: "That" (or which) introduces extra information about a THING: the story that we read. "Where" is only for a PLACE (the park where we played).
why.zh: that（或 which）引出关于东西的补充信息：the story that we read。where 只用于地点（the park where we played）。

what where.en: Two question words together is never correct. A story is a thing, so that.
what where.zh: 两个疑问词放在一起永远不对。故事是东西，所以用 that。

where.en: "Where" is for places. A story is not a place, so that.
where.zh: where 用于地点。故事不是地点，所以用 that。

where it.en: "Where" is for places, and "it" repeats the story twice. Use: the story that we read.
where it.zh: where 用于地点，而且 it 又重复了一次 story。用 the story that we read。

questions.q: Is everything (all right / allright)?

why.en: "All right" is two separate words, like "all wrong". That is the standard spelling in school writing.
why.zh: all right 是两个分开的词，就像 all wrong。这是学校写作的标准拼法。

allright.en: All right is two words. Joining them into one is a spelling mistake.
allright.zh: all right 是两个词，连成一个词是拼写错误。

al right.en: "All" has two Ls. "Al" is not a word.
al right.zh: all 有两个 l。al 不是一个词。

alright right.en: This repeats "right" twice. Just: all right.
alright right.zh: 这样 right 重复了两次。只写 all right。

questions.q: Emma (teaches / learns) her little brother to swim.

why.en: A teacher TEACHES (gives the knowledge). A student LEARNS (gets the knowledge). Emma is giving the lesson, so Emma teaches. And "Emma" is one person (he/she), so add -es: teaches.
why.zh: 老师 teaches（教，给出知识），学生 learns（学，得到知识）。Emma 在教，所以用 teaches。Emma 是一个人（第三人称单数），加 -es：teaches。

learn.en: "Learn" is what the student does, and it also needs -s with Emma. Emma is the one teaching.
learn.zh: learn 是学生做的事，而且 Emma 后面要加 -s。Emma 是教的人。

learns.en: Her little brother learns; Emma teaches. You cannot "learn someone" something in correct English.
learns.zh: 弟弟是 learns，Emma 是 teaches。正确的英语不能说 learn someone 某事。

teach him learns.en: This puts two verbs together and adds an extra "him". One verb is enough: Emma teaches her little brother.
teach him learns.zh: 这样两个动词放在一起，还多了 him。一个动词就够了：Emma teaches her little brother。

questions.q: The puppy wagged (its / it's) tail.

why.en: "Its" (no apostrophe) shows the tail belongs to the puppy. Possessive pronouns (his, her, its, their) never have an apostrophe.
why.zh: its（没有撇号）表示尾巴是小狗的。物主代词（his、her、its、their）都没有撇号。

it is.en: "The puppy wagged it is tail" makes no sense. We need a word that shows belonging.
it is.zh: The puppy wagged it is tail 说不通，我们需要表示所属的词。

it's.en: It's = it is (or it has). Read it out: "wagged it is tail" is wrong, so not it's.
it's.zh: it's = it is（或 it has）。读出来：wagged it is tail 不对，所以不是 it's。

its'.en: Its' does not exist in English. The possessive is just its.
its'.zh: 英语里没有 its'，物主形式就是 its。

title.en: Homework: Rock Layers and Ocean Floor

intro.en: Read Main Book S4 to S6 first. Then do this. You can try again as many times as you like.
intro.zh: 先读主课本 S4 到 S6，再做（可以做很多次）。

canNow.en: I can now answer rock layer and ocean floor questions on my own.
canNow.zh: 我现在可以自己回答岩层和海底的问题。

questions.q: Who wrote Theory of the Earth in 1795?

why.en: James Hutton, a Scottish geologist, wrote Theory of the Earth in 1795. He saw that slow processes like erosion and deposition shape Earth over a very long time, so he is called the father of modern geology.
why.zh: 苏格兰地质学家詹姆斯·赫顿在 1795 年写了《地球理论》。他发现侵蚀和沉积这些缓慢的过程在很长时间里塑造了地球，所以被称为现代地质学之父。

Isaac Newton.en: Newton was a scientist of gravity and light, and he died in 1727, before 1795.
Isaac Newton.zh: 牛顿研究的是重力和光，他在 1727 年就去世了，早于 1795 年。

Charles Darwin.en: Darwin wrote about evolution (how living things change), and he was born in 1809, after 1795.
Charles Darwin.zh: 达尔文写的是进化论（生物如何变化），他 1809 年才出生，晚于 1795 年。

Albert Einstein.en: Einstein was a physicist born in 1879, almost 100 years later.
Albert Einstein.zh: 爱因斯坦是物理学家，1879 年出生，晚了将近 100 年。

questions.q: Uplift means...

why.en: Uplift raises land up. Weathering and erosion wear it down.
why.zh: 抬升让土地升高，风化和侵蚀把它磨低。

rain falling.en: Rain falling is precipitation. Uplift is land being pushed UP.
rain falling.zh: 下雨是降水。uplift 是陆地被往上推。

dropping sediment.en: Dropping sediment is deposition, which builds land low down, not mountains.
dropping sediment.zh: 放下沉积物是沉积，在低处堆积，不是造山。

wearing rock down.en: Wearing rock down is weathering and erosion, the opposite of uplift.
wearing rock down.zh: 把岩石磨低是风化和侵蚀，和抬升正相反。

questions.q: Sedimentary rock forms when layers of sediment are...

why.en: Compacted (pressed) and cemented (stuck) together.
why.zh: 被压紧和粘合在一起。

frozen in a glacier.en: Freezing does not make rock. When the ice melts, the sediment is still loose.
frozen in a glacier.zh: 冻起来不会变成岩石。冰一化，沉积物还是松散的。

blown away by wind.en: Blowing away is erosion. The sediment must stay and be pressed together to become rock.
blown away by wind.zh: 被吹走是侵蚀。沉积物要留下来被压紧才能变成岩石。

melted by magma.en: Rock that melts and cools becomes IGNEOUS rock, not sedimentary.
melted by magma.zh: 熔化后冷却的岩石是火成岩，不是沉积岩。

questions.q: Layer 1 is at the bottom and layer 3 is at the top. Which is the youngest?

why.en: Superposition: each new layer of sediment is laid down ON TOP of the older ones. Layer 3 was put down last, so it is the youngest.
why.zh: 叠加原理：每一层新的沉积物都盖在旧的上面。第 3 层是最后放下的，所以最年轻。

they are the same age.en: Layers are laid down one after another, so each one is a different age.
they are the same age.zh: 岩层是一层一层先后堆的，所以每层年龄不同。

layer 2.en: Layer 2 is in the middle. Layer 3 was laid on top of it later, so 3 is younger.
layer 2.zh: 第 2 层在中间，第 3 层后来盖在它上面，所以第 3 层更年轻。

layer 1.en: Layer 1 is at the bottom. It was laid down FIRST, so it is the OLDEST.
layer 1.zh: 第 1 层在最底下，是最先形成的，所以最老。

questions.q: "Super" in superposition means...

why.en: "Super" comes from Latin and means ABOVE or over (like superhero = above a normal hero, Superman flies above). Superposition = the position ABOVE: younger layers lie above older ones.
why.zh: super 来自拉丁语，意思是“在上面、超过”（superhero 超级英雄、Superman 在天上飞）。superposition = 在上面的位置：新的岩层在老的岩层上面。

below.en: Below is the opposite of super. The word for below is "sub" (submarine goes under the sea).
below.zh: below 是 super 的反义。表示“在下面”的是 sub（submarine 潜水艇在水下）。

old.en: Super does not mean old. The idea is about position: which layer is above.
old.zh: super 不是“老”的意思，它讲的是位置：哪层在上面。

same.en: Super does not mean same. The word for same is "uni" or "homo" (uniform = same form).
same.zh: super 不是“相同”的意思。表示相同的是 uni（uniform = 相同的形状）。

questions.q: A cutaway view of the rocks in one place is called a...

why.en: Like cutting a layer cake to see inside.
why.zh: 像切开千层蛋糕看里面。

station model.en: A station model is a weather map symbol, not a view of rocks.
station model.zh: 站点模型是天气图上的符号，不是看岩石的图。

drainage basin.en: A drainage basin is an area of land that drains into one river.
drainage basin.zh: 流域是一片流进同一条河的土地。

delta.en: A delta is land built at a river mouth, not a picture of rock layers.
delta.zh: 三角洲是河口堆积的陆地，不是岩层的图。

questions.q: The continental rise is covered by...
options: sediment from the shelf and slope

why.en: Sediment drifted down and settled at the bottom of the slope.
why.zh: 沉积物飘下来，堆在大陆坡底部。

glaciers.en: Glaciers are on land in very cold places, not on the deep sea floor.
glaciers.zh: 冰川在很冷的陆地上，不在深海底。

magma.en: Magma comes up at ridges and volcanoes. The rise is a pile of sediment that slid down.
magma.zh: 岩浆从洋脊和火山冒出来。大陆隆是滑下来的沉积物堆。

coral only.en: Coral grows in shallow, warm, sunny water, not thousands of metres deep.
coral only.zh: 珊瑚长在浅、暖、有阳光的水里，不在几千米深的地方。

questions.q: An active margin, like the west coast of North America, often has...
options: a narrow shelf, trenches, volcanoes and earthquakes
a very wide shelf and no earthquakes

why.en: Active = plate boundary nearby.
why.zh: 主动 = 附近有板块边界。

a very wide shelf and no earthquakes.en: That is a PASSIVE margin, with no plate boundary nearby.
a very wide shelf and no earthquakes.zh: 那是被动大陆边缘，附近没有板块边界。

no ocean at all.en: A margin is the edge where land meets ocean, so there is always ocean.
no ocean at all.zh: 大陆边缘就是陆地和海洋相接的地方，所以一定有海。

only sand dunes.en: Sand dunes are built by wind. Active margins are about plate movement.
only sand dunes.zh: 沙丘是风堆的。活动大陆边缘讲的是板块运动。

questions.q: Deep-sea trenches are...

why.en: Trenches are the deepest parts of the ocean.
why.zh: 海沟是海洋最深的地方。

the highest mountains.en: Trenches go DOWN, deeper than Mount Everest is tall. They are the opposite of high.
the highest mountains.zh: 海沟是往下的，比珠穆朗玛峰的高度还深，和“高”正相反。

river mouths.en: River mouths are where rivers reach the sea, at sea level, and they build deltas.
river mouths.zh: 河口是河流入海处，在海平面，会形成三角洲。

flat plains.en: Flat deep floor is the abyssal plain. Trenches are narrow and V-shaped.
flat plains.zh: 平坦的深海底是深海平原。海沟是窄的 V 形。

questions.q: Mid-ocean ridges form at...
options: divergent boundaries, where plates move apart

why.en: Diverge = move apart.
why.zh: diverge = 分开。

the North Pole only.en: Ridges run through every ocean, about 60,000 km in all, not only at the North Pole.
the North Pole only.zh: 洋脊穿过每一个大洋，总长约 6 万公里，不只在北极。

convergent boundaries, where plates coll.en: Colliding plates make trenches and mountains. Ridges form where plates move APART.
convergent boundaries, where plates coll.zh: 板块相撞形成海沟和山脉。洋脊在板块分开的地方形成。

the shoreline.en: The shoreline is the edge of the land. Ridges are in the middle of the ocean.
the shoreline.zh: 海岸线是陆地的边缘。洋脊在大洋中间。

intro.en: Read the word, say what it means, then tap to check.
intro.zh: 读词，说出意思，再点卡片检查。

cards.back: What the air is like today: hot or cold, wet or dry, windy or calm.
cards.zhBack: 今天空气的样子：冷热、干湿、有没有风。

cards.back: The usual weather of a place over many years.
cards.zhBack: 一个地方很多年来通常的天气。

cards.back: The layer of air around Earth.
A huge body of air with the same temperature and wetness all through.
cards.zhBack: 温度和湿度都差不多的一大团空气。

cards.back: Hot: made near the equator.
Cold: made near the poles.
Wet: made over the ocean.
Dry: made over land.
The line where two different air masses meet.
cards.zhBack: 两种不同气团相遇的地方。

cards.back: Cold air pushes under warm air fast, like a bulldozer: sudden storms.
cards.zhBack: 冷空气像推土机一样快速钻到暖空气下面：突然的暴风雨。

cards.back: Warm air slides slowly up over cold air, like a ramp: gentle rain for a long time.
cards.zhBack: 暖空气像走斜坡一样慢慢滑到冷空气上面：长时间小雨。

cards.back: Water vapour (a gas) turning back into liquid drops.
cards.zhBack: 水蒸气（气体）变回小水滴。

canNow.en: I can now explain 12 weather words.
canNow.zh: 我现在能解释 12 个天气词汇。

intro.en: Tap a word, then tap its meaning.

pairs.b: today
many years
wet, over the ocean
dry, over land
hot, near the equator
cold, near the poles
the bulldozer: sudden storms
the ramp: gentle rain
